required_audit_coverage.name: required_audit_coverage
required_audit_coverage.detail: report covers all 35 Required Audit items with substantive aligned answers
required_audit_items: Was `project_state/decision_packet.md` treated as the only task authority?
Was `project_state/task_packet.json` treated as background only?
Did `decision_meta` remain valid, `APPROVED`, and aligned with active `reverse-agent-iteration@v2`?
Was the previous accepted manual-mode orchestrator round treated as the baseline?
Were existing project_gate/report/job/orchestrator capabilities inspected before adding new governance code?
Did the implementation avoid duplicating existing prompt docs, policy-lint, prompt-consistency, command-plan, execution-log, report-summary, and closeout mechanisms?
Was `project_state/state_manifest.json` generated?
Does `state_manifest.json` carry current decision, round, report, pytest, command-plan, execution-log, final-check, and closeout references?
Does `state_manifest.json` classify current, generated, historical_nonblocking, archived, missing, and optional artifacts without treating historical missing sample artifacts as blockers?
Does `state_manifest.json` preserve `project_state` files as audit fact sources rather than replacing them?
Was `project_state/context/current_context_packet.json` generated?

Does `current_context_packet.json` summarize current authority, mainline, accepted baseline, state digest, artifact freshness, negative-results constraints, existing capabilities, forbidden capabilities, and stop conditions?
Does `current_context_packet.json` avoid embedding large file contents, full solve reports, or dynamic facts in prompt/skill files?
Was `project_state/roadmap/workstreams.json` generated?
Does `workstreams.json` use the required lifecycle states?
Does `workstreams.json` mark only this governance round as active, if any workstream is active?
Does `workstreams.json` keep User Solve Layer, AgentRunner, CI, Web, database/indexing, state hygiene, reverse solving, and tool integration as separate workstreams rather than mixing them?
Does the workstream registry make clear that roadmap entries are not execution authority until selected by `decision_packet.md`?
Was project-gate integration added for governance context validation?
Did the gate generate `project_state/gates/project_governance_context_result.json` or equivalent current artifact?
Did the gate generate `project_state/gates/project_governance_context_snapshot.json` or equivalent current snapshot?
Do all new gate artifacts carry current decision/report/round IDs?
Did command-plan authorize every executed command?
Were command-plan omitted commands left unexecuted?
Did pytest_result record real commands and exit codes?
Did focused tests cover state manifest, context packet, workstream registry, and gate validation?
Did broad project gate/report tests continue to pass?
Did final-check pass with current IDs?
Did report-summary synthesis pass and match the report summary?
Did run-closeout pass if authorized?
Were forbidden files untouched?
Were `.github/workflows/*`, `.codex-skills/*`, `solve_reports/*`, and real sample directories untouched?
Did the implementation avoid model API calls, runner dispatch, external tool execution, database/queue creation, Web service creation, CI dispatch, and auto-iteration?
Did the final report avoid any solved/static/runtime/audit verification claim for concrete samples?
Did the final report explicitly state that `state_manifest`, `current_context_packet`, and `workstreams` are indexes/governance artifacts, not audit fact replacements?
